record.final_answer:
The key knob in Thistlewire 0.9 is `max_buffered_messages`, set per server-streaming call. From the docs note I have stored (thistlewire.example/docs/streaming): 0.9 has no built-in flow control for server streaming — the server queues for a slow client without bound, and `max_buffered_messages` defaults to 0, meaning unlimited. That default is precisely your balloon: one dashboard that stops reading gets an ever-growing queue until memory or the box gives out.

So:

1. Set a finite `max_buffered_messages` on the new streaming handler. This is the only backpressure boundary you get on the server side, because there is no client-driven window in 0.9.

2. Size it in ticks, not bytes — it counts messages, and a tick is tiny. Pick the smaller of two budgets: how much memory you'll let one stalled dashboard pin, and how much backlog a merely jittery client should be allowed to work off before you give up on it. A few hundred to a thousand ticks gives a flaky Wi-Fi client a few seconds of grace while keeping per-stream memory in the tens-to-hundreds of KB; tunable once you know your tick rate.

3. Know the overflow semantics: at the cap the stream is closed with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. There is no drop-oldest option, so a slow client doesn't get stale ticks — it gets disconnected. Design the dashboard side for that: on RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, reconnect and resnapshot with the existing unary `prices.Get`, then resubscribe. Without that, a Wi-Fi hiccup silently leaves a dashboard frozen.

4. Watch stream multiplication. If there's no server-side cap on concurrent streams (I couldn't confirm one — the package isn't installed in this environment and the docs domain 404s from here), a browser reconnect loop can hold N buffers per dashboard. Give the client reconnect jitter/backoff.

5. Keep the producer loop non-blocking: with N dashboards fed from one tick loop, bounded queues mean one overflow only closes that one stream — make sure the fan-out doesn't await a slow subscriber inline.

Caveat: requirements.txt pins 0.9.4, and my note is on the 0.9 docs. Confirm the option name and whether it's per-stream or per-call in your installed version before wiring it in — nothing in `server.py` today needs changing yet.
